title: A first continuous distribution

prereqs.why: This is the first problem where probabilities come from an area rather than a sum.
The variable is continuous, which changes what a distribution even is.

statement:
A bus arrives at a time $T$ **uniformly distributed** on the interval $[0, 20]$ minutes after you arrive. Its density is

$$f(t) = \begin{cases} \tfrac1{20} & 0 \le t \le 20 \\ 0 & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}$$

You give up and leave if the bus has not come within $5$ minutes.

What is $\P(T \le 5)$?

Give your answer as a **decimal, rounded to two decimal places** — this one is checked approximately, to a tolerance of $\pm 0.005$, rather than exactly.
hints: For a continuous variable, a probability is the area under the density over the region you care about — not a sum of probabilities of individual values.
The density is flat at $\tfrac1{20}$ between $0$ and $20$. The region you want is $0 \le t \le 5$, which is a rectangle.

payload.prompt: The probability that the bus arrives within five minutes.
payload.label: $\P(T \le 5) =$
payload.syntax: A decimal, to two decimal places. Checked to within ±0.005.
